source_row.rationale: Maternal rubella infection, particularly during the first trimester when fetal organ development is most vulnerable, carries a significant risk of congenital rubella syndrome, which can cause serious birth defects, including cardiac defects, cataracts/other eye abnormalities, and sensorineural hearing loss — underscoring the importance of rubella immunity confirmation before pregnancy, since the live MMR vaccine cannot be given during pregnancy itself.
